title: Carson Static — Deconstructed Grunge Spread
description: A full-throated tribute to David Carson's Ray Gun era: type fractured and overprinted, photographs rotated against the grain, body copy bleeding deliberately off-canvas. Unlike tidy maximalist templates, this one treats every grid violation as a load-bearing design decision.
philosophy: This template exists on the conviction that legibility is not always the point — tension, texture, and visual aggression communicate what clean grids cannot. It inherits the 1990s belief that layout itself is content: a body block running into the gutter says something a centered headline never could. It refuses hierarchy, decorative restraint, and the quiet authority of baseline alignment. It is built for speakers who treat the slide surface as an artifact rather than a delivery mechanism.
goodFor: Design portfolio and creative retrospective presentations
Music, subculture, or countercultural brand pitches
Art school thesis defenses and experimental studio critiques
avoidFor: Quarterly financial reviews requiring legible multi-column data tables
Medical or clinical research presentations with dense body text
Enterprise software sales decks targeting compliance-conscious buyers
Public-sector presentations held to WCAG accessibility standards
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a spread torn from a mid-nineties underground music zine — raw, confrontational, and deliberately uncomfortable. Photographic texture competes with typographic mass rather than supporting it; the title does not sit, it collides. Compositional rhythm is dense-chaotic with a single deliberate anchor point to prevent total dissolution. Avoid any suggestion of centering, symmetry, or decorative calm — visual aggression is the hierarchy.

examples.layoutNotes: No enforced outer margin — the deck title is set at extreme scale, rotated roughly 12° counter-clockwise, anchored to the bottom-left quadrant and deliberately severed by the left canvas edge. A subtitle or deck-context fragment overprints at approximately 40% opacity in the upper-right quadrant, colliding with a torn or skewed photographic element occupying the top 55% of the canvas. One small upright text anchor (deck name, date, or sequence number) sits bottom-right as the sole composed, readable element. Layering order: photograph bleeds beneath the giant title type, subtitle fragment overprints both.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a photocopied zine page — raw, physically handled, almost confrontational. Compositional rhythm is dense and colliding: multiple text layers coexist at competing scales and angles, none deferring to the other. A torn-edge photographic fragment anchors one zone while body copy invades it without apology. Mood is underground-aggressive, channeling deliberate illegibility as editorial voice; avoid tidy hierarchy, decorative softness, or any resolved negative space.

examples.layoutNotes: Implicit 12-column grid, actively violated: the primary body block occupies cols 1–7 but rotates roughly 8° counter-clockwise, its left edge clipping into the gutter bleed. A secondary text fragment — overprinted pull quote or lone fractured word — spans cols 8–12 and bleeds off the right canvas edge entirely. A photographic element fills the upper-right quadrant, tilted against the body text's grain with no spatial buffer separating type from image. No header band; page locator stamped small at an unexpected interior position, overprinted directly on imagery.
